name: Customer Advisory Board Problem Council
phase: Customer Discovery and Problem Validation Tactics
hypothesis: We believe that [industry vertical] executives consider [nascent regulatory or operational challenge] a board-level risk. We will verify this by hosting a 6-executive roundtable, and consider it validated if ≥ 4 members confirm they have formally committed budget to mitigate the issue in the current fiscal year.

plan.label: Preparation
plan.text: Recruit six non-competing executives and frame the session as an off-the-record working council.

plan.label: Execution
plan.text: Under the Chatham House Rule, have each name their single greatest vulnerability, with no product pitch.

plan.label: Data collection
plan.text: Record how peers validate each other, which budget lines are disclosed, and which problems recur.

planFull.label: Preparation
planFull.text: Recruit 6 non-competing industry executives. Frame the session as an off-the-record working council on emerging operational bottlenecks.

planFull.label: Execution
planFull.text: Facilitate an executive Chatham House Rule discussion around operational risks. Require each participant to detail their single greatest vulnerability without evaluating potential software solutions.

planFull.label: Data collection
planFull.text: Record the level of inter-participant validation, specific budget line items disclosed, and shared operational challenges that surface organically across accounts.

warning.label: Executive Echo Chamber
warning.text: Executives echo industry buzzwords to look forward-thinking before peers, regardless of budget.

warningFull: Board members often echo high-level industry buzzwords and macro narratives to appear forward-thinking before peers, irrespective of actual internal budget allocation.
